text:
The forward‑scattering amplitude is  

\[
f(0)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l=0}^{4}(2l+1)\bigl(e^{2i\delta_l}-1\bigr)
      =\frac{1}{k}\sum_{l=0}^{4}(2l+1)e^{i\delta_l}\sin\delta_l .
\]

Its imaginary part is therefore  

\[
\operatorname{Im}f(0)=\frac{1}{k}\sum_{l=0}^{4}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\!\delta_l .
\]

Using the given phase shifts (in degrees)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin^{2}\!90^{\circ}&=1,\\
\sin^{2}\!67^{\circ}&\approx0.848,\\
\sin^{2}\!55^{\circ}&\approx0.671,\\
\sin^{2}\!30^{\circ}&=0.25,\\
\sin^{2}\!13^{\circ}&\approx0.0506,
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\!\delta_l
=1(1)+3(0.848)+5(0.671)+7(0.25)+9(0.0506)
\approx 9.10 .
\]

For a 50 MeV electron the relativistic wave‑number is  

\[
k=\frac{\sqrt{(T+m_e)^2-m_e^{2}}}{\hbar c}
   =\frac{50.5\;\text{MeV}}{197.3\;\text{MeV·fm}}
   \approx 0.256\;\text{fm}^{-1}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\operatorname{Im}f(0)=\frac{9.10}{0.256}\;\text{fm}
                     \approx 3.55\times10^{2}\;\text{fm}.
\]

The value that matches this result is  

**Answer: B**.
